name: Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit
summary: Overnight stays outside the specifically exempt areas are prohibited.
vehicleRule: An open road or parking space does not authorize sleeping in the car. Forest Order 19-24-05 lists the exempt areas and limits and runs through December 1, 2027. Those exceptions are not fully digitized here.
exceptions: Use only the exempt locations in Exhibits A and B and comply with their stay limits.
Order effective June 28, 2024 through December 1, 2027; later orders may replace it.
scope: Forest policy; exact pullout permission still requires local checks

name: Eldorado National Forest
summary: Roadside dispersed camping is generally permitted on eligible Forest Service land.
vehicleRule: Park on an existing durable spot within one vehicle length of an open designated road. Keep the sleeping location at least 100 feet from water. Limit: 10 days per ranger district per calendar year.
exceptions: Choose a spot at least 100 feet from lakes and streams.
Stay outside developed-campground boundaries; current orders and seasonal road closures still apply.
The annual-limit order has separate exceptions for specified wilderness areas and the Pacific Crest Trail.
scope: Forest policy; exact pullout permission still requires local checks

name: Inyo National Forest
summary: Dispersed camping is permitted outside Restricted Recreation Areas.
vehicleRule: Keep the car on established roads; off-road driving to camp is prohibited. Stay at least 200 feet from water. Limit: 14 consecutive days at one location, 28 days per calendar year across the forest; move at least 10 miles.
exceptions: At least 200 feet from water.
Within Restricted Recreation Areas, camping is limited to developed campground campsites or posted overflow areas.
Order 05-04-50-25-17 runs through July 3, 2027; local closures may add restrictions.

sources.label: Camping guidance and interactive restricted-area map

scope: Forest policy; exact pullout permission still requires local checks

name: Tahoe National Forest
summary: Camping is prohibited within the mapped east-side and Highway 20 restricted areas, except specified sites and exemptions.
vehicleRule: Truckee/Sierraville restrictions include roads and trails. Highway 20 has mapped quarter-mile and half-mile buffers and Conservation Camp Road restrictions. The app has not yet digitized those exclusions, so an exact roadside verdict here remains unknown.
exceptions: East-side restricted areas: approved campgrounds/designated dispersed sites and specified trail corridors only; a hiking-corridor exemption does not authorize driving there.
Highway 20: mapped half-mile and quarter-mile buffers and Conservation Camp Road restrictions under Order 17-25-01.
The Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit has its own more restrictive overnight order.
scope: Forest policy; exact pullout permission still requires local checks

name: Mendocino National Forest
summary: Dispersed camping is permitted outside developed sites and their one-mile exclusion buffers.
vehicleRule: Use an existing impacted site beside an open vehicle route, at least 150 feet from water. No universal off-road distance was established. At the same one-mile-radius location: 14 days per 30 days and 28 days per 12 months.
exceptions: Remain at least 150 feet from water.
Developed recreation sites include campgrounds, picnic areas and trailheads; the one-mile exclusion matters even when an adjacent road is open.
Within the same one-mile-radius location: at most 14 days in any 30-day period and 28 cumulative days in any 12-month period.
scope: Forest policy; exact pullout permission still requires local checks

name: Shasta-Trinity National Forest
summary: The published guidance does not clearly settle sleeping inside a roadside car.
vehicleRule: Parking is limited to one vehicle length from a designated road, but camps are required to be at least 200 feet from roads. Those two instructions do not establish a yes for sleeping in the parked car; this map therefore marks it unknown.
exceptions: No dispersed camping at Lewiston Lake or in the Mt. Shasta plantations area.
Other exclusions include restricted nesting areas and mapped no-camping zones.
Published guidance also separates camps from developed sites, trailheads, private property and state highways.
scope: Forest policy; exact pullout permission still requires local checks

name: Sierra National Forest
summary: Dispersed camping is generally described as available, but roadside vehicle sleeping is not explicitly settled.
vehicleRule: The researched forest sources do not give a universal car-sleeping or pull-off rule. This app keeps the exact roadside permission unknown rather than applying another forest’s distance limit.
exceptions: Opening and closing dates can change without notice for weather or safety.
Exact ownership and current closure coverage remain unresolved at a selected point.
scope: Forest policy; exact pullout permission still requires local checks

name: Plumas National Forest
summary: The sources establish camping limits but do not establish blanket roadside car-sleeping permission.
vehicleRule: Dispersed limit: 14 days per ranger district per calendar year; 30 total camping days per year across the forest. A campsite is limited to eight people and two vehicles. A universal roadside pull-off distance was not established.
exceptions: Dispersed camping is limited to 14 days per ranger district per calendar year; total forest camping is limited to 30 days per calendar year.
Individual campsites are limited to eight people and two vehicles.
Occupancy limits do not by themselves authorize roadside sleeping.
scope: Forest policy; exact pullout permission still requires local checks

name: Stanislaus National Forest
summary: Roadside dispersed camping is permitted outside developed recreation areas and other posted restrictions.
vehicleRule: Park within one vehicle length of the designated forest transportation route, using an existing site. Keep camp at least 150 feet from water. Limit: 21 days per ranger district per calendar year.
exceptions: Keep camps at least 150 feet from streams or other water.
Dispersed camping is typically not allowed near developed campgrounds, picnic areas or trailheads.
Current closures, Cherry Lake restrictions, fire rules and seasonal access may add restrictions.
scope: Forest policy; exact pullout permission still requires local checks

name: Gifford Pinchot National Forest
summary: Motorized dispersed camping is permitted only along designated camping corridors.
vehicleRule: Use an existing route within 150 feet of the main road, in a highway-legal vehicle. Do not create a track. Keep at least 100 feet from water. This app has not yet digitized the camping-corridor tables.
exceptions: Some roads do not permit motorized access to dispersed camps; absent corridor symbols do not grant access.
Stay at least 100 feet from water and out of fragile meadows/restricted areas.
After 14 consecutive camping days, leave the forest; current closures still apply.
scope: Forest policy; exact pullout permission still requires local checks

name: Mt. Hood National Forest
summary: Dispersed camping is supported outside developed and restricted areas; exact roadside car sleeping is unresolved.
vehicleRule: Use an existing impacted site, at least 100 feet from water. Limits: 14 consecutive days at one location and 28 days forest-wide per calendar year. Some roads and sensitive areas are closed to camping; a blanket pull-off distance was not established.
exceptions: Camping is closed in developed recreation sites, along some roads and in sensitive areas; the full set of exclusions is not mapped here.
Camp at least 100 feet from streams, rivers and lakes.
Maximum 14 consecutive days in one location and 28 days forest-wide per calendar year.
scope: Forest policy; exact pullout permission still requires local checks

name: Deschutes National Forest
summary: Motorized dispersed camping requires a route designated for that use.
vehicleRule: The historical travel decision permits up to 300 feet on eligible routes, at existing or designated sites and no closer than 30 feet to water. Current route-specific and area restrictions are not fully digitized here.
exceptions: Routes absent from the current MVUM are not open to public motor vehicles.
Current area closures, including active alerts around Bend, can override the underlying travel designation.
Do not create tracks or treat an open driving road as automatic camping permission.
scope: Forest policy; exact pullout permission still requires local checks

name: Coconino National Forest
summary: Car camping is supported only on road segments designated for dispersed camping.
vehicleRule: The allowance is up to 300 feet from the edge of a designated camping road, on National Forest System land. It does not apply to every open driving road. This app has not yet digitized those corridor designations.
exceptions: The travel map identifies prohibited camping locations in Flagstaff and Sedona city limits.
Check current MVUM, forest orders and local designated-site-only restrictions before using a pullout.
Keep the traveled roadway clear; an open road without camping designation is not evidence of vehicle-camping access.
scope: Forest policy; exact pullout permission still requires local checks

name: Uinta-Wasatch-Cache National Forest
summary: Roadside vehicle camping depends on the exact ranger district and designated road segment.
vehicleRule: Pleasant Grove’s 2025 map allows 150 feet from road centerline only on specifically listed roads, with side-of-road and vehicle/season limits. That distance does not apply forest-wide. Corridor designations are not yet digitized here.
exceptions: The map distinguishes left-side, right-side and both-side camping corridors.
Other districts have their own maps and tables; never extend the Pleasant Grove allowance to another district.
Current camping restrictions, water setbacks and emergency closures remain separate checks.
scope: Forest policy; exact pullout permission still requires local checks

name: White River National Forest
summary: Roadside dispersed camping is permitted, with designated-site-only exceptions in some areas.
vehicleRule: Use an already impacted site within 300 feet of the road centerline, at least 100 feet from water. General limit: 14 days per 30 days, then move outside a 20-mile radius. Some areas instead require designated sites or a seven-day limit.
exceptions: Some locations restrict dispersed camping to designated sites or seven-day stays.
Unless otherwise noted, maximum 14 days within 30 days, then relocate outside a 20-mile radius.
Site-specific regulations, current orders and seasonal access override general guidance.
scope: Forest policy; exact pullout permission still requires local checks
